news.title: Football: Soccer-Scaloni extends contract as Argentina head coach until 2030
news.lede: Nov 12 (Reuters) - Lionel Scaloni ⁠has extended his contract as Argentina head coach until ⁠July 2030, the Argentine Football Association said on ‌Thursday. Scaloni, who guided Argentina to the 2022 World Cup title and two Copa America triumphs, had castdoubt on his future after Argentina’s World Cup final ​defeat to Spain in July, with his ⁠deal set to expire ⁠in December 2026. But the Argentine has agreed to new terms ⁠with the ‌national side, extending his stay until 2030. “We are going to officially announce the renewal of Lionel ⁠Scaloni's coaching staff for the period from 2027 ​to 2030 at ‌the helm of the Argentine National Team," AFA president ⁠Claudio Tapia told ​reporters.

news.title: FIFA's 2031 Women's World Cup could make history with four host nations and 48 teams
news.lede: The Briefing: FIFA published its bid evaluation report on November 11, finding the joint U.S.-Mexico-Costa Rica-Jamaica submission for the 2031 Women's World Cup meets minimum hosting requirements with a score of 4.4 out of 5 — the only bid received for that edition. An Extraordinary FIFA Congress will convene by videoconference on November 23, 2026, so all 211 member associations can vote to formally award hosting rights for the 2031 and 2035 Women's World Cups. If approved, the 2031 tournament will be the first Women's World Cup hosted across four nations simultaneously, featuring 48 teams and 104 matches — 40 more than the 2023 edition in Australia and New Zealand. Eleven days from now, 211 FIFA member associations will log on for a virtual vote that is poised to deliver the most consequential decision in the history of women's football.

news.title: EPL, World Cup, now Hall of Fame: Garcia’s legacy grows
news.lede: Few West Australians have hit the same heights Richard Garcia did during his football career. Even fewer have been able to parlay that experience and love of the world game into a coaching career shaping the next generation. And if it was a love of the world game which took a wide-eyed, 15 year-old Garcia from Perth to England, it was the same endearment which kept him over there almost a decade-and-a-half and has sustained him in his second act as a coach. “I don’t think I ever thought of anything else except football — I still don’t really consider anything except football now,” Garcia told The West Australian.

news.title: Ex-Cameroon striker Raphael Messi Bouli discusses Samuel Eto’o, World Cup ambitions before AFCON 2027 qualifiers
news.lede: Chennai Until recently, Cameroon had been one of the most consistent sides from Africa to feature in the FIFA World Cup. Between 1982 and 2014, across nine editions, it played in seven of them. But in the last three editions, it has missed the berth twice. Its legend, Samuel Eto’o, has made headlines for the wrong reasons as president of the Cameroon FA, and the Indomitable Lions find themselves lost in the savannah, looking for a stage to roar again.

news.title: Hundreds of England fans arrested for football disorder during World Cup — but most on home soil
news.lede: Hundreds of of England football thugs were arrested on home soil for disorder during the World Cup, new figures reveal. Home Office data shows there were 19 arrests of travelling England fans during the 2026 tournament. In total, 16 arrests were made in the United States, three arrests were made in Mexico and no arrests were made in Canada. But in England and Wales, there were 357 football-related arrests for Three Lions supporters during the tournament.
